title: First P12 rerun chain was started, then aborted a minute in because further frozen-tool edits were planned
what_went_wrong: The chain (session P12-RERUN-20261024) was started on the run-lock bytes, then stopped about one minute into its fixture build because the STRATA pin and the new tools would change frozen bytes again; running a 2 h chain on bytes about to change would have produced evidence for the wrong set.

My first kill attempt used pkill -f with a pattern that also matched my own ssh command line, which killed the ssh session; the suite processes survived and were stopped with plain kill (SIGTERM) so their traps ran.
root_cause: The chain was launched before the full list of frozen-byte changes for the wave was decided.
impact: No evidence was produced or cited from the aborted run. Cleanup under a held lock (session CLEANUP-20261024): fixture sik_p6f dropped with --teardown-kept, no writer marker, no benchmark grant on the fixture, both database.xml on sik, databases sik and sik_bench only. The lock was released.

correction.applied: Decided all frozen-byte changes first, deployed them, froze manifest 20261024b, then started one chain (P12-RERUN-20261024B).
correction.result: Chain 20261024T112518Z ran uncontended on the final bytes.

rule: Decide the complete set of frozen-byte changes before starting an evidence chain; never kill with pkill -f patterns that match the caller's own command line.
